Subject: Renewal & capacity + hw-class upgrade question

Hi Priya / Avery,

We're coming up on our Oct renewal and Procurement has asked us to evaluate a hardware-class upgrade for our Dedicated pool: we currently run primarily A100 reserved GPUs and want to understand the case for moving to H100 or L40S (or a mixed pool) for the same or slightly higher spend. Key asks from Procurement:
- A clear performance-per-dollar analysis for our workload (LLM text generation + embeddings)
- Throughput guarantees / SLOs if we commit to a reserved increment (we're looking at +40 GPUs)
- Migration window, rollback plan, and any required model re-quantization work

I've attached our June usage slice (acme_current_usage_202607.csv). Can you put together a short proposal (numbers, suggested term length, pricing, and a sample ROI calc)? Procurement would like this by EOD Thursday so they can start redlines.

Thanks,
Jenna Park

Acme.ai

Hi Jenna — thanks for the clear asks and the usage file. Attached is an initial proposal and benchmark summary (redwood_h100_l40s_ppd_model_benchmarks.pdf and renewal_quote_ACME_v3.xlsx). High-level summary up front:

- Proposal: +40 reserved GPUs (mix: 30x H100 + 10x L40S) for a 12-month term with a stepped price model. We can offer a throughput SLA for generation capacity: 99% of requests below 120ms token latency for short prompt workloads (<=1024 tokens) and a 99.9% reserved throughput guarantee of X tokens/sec across the pool at baseline load.

- Performance-per-dollar: for your current model mix (gpt-like 16B variants + embedding models), H100 shows ~1.9x tokens/sec vs A100 at the same batch/seq; L40S gives ~1.6x for embeddings and better memory density for large contexts. After accounting for expected average utilization from your June slice (avg pool utilization 72%), the blended cost/token for the proposed H100/L40S mix is ~22% lower than continuing to expand on A100 alone (detailed calc in the quote).

- Migration plan: staged roll (canary 4 GPUs of H100 for 7 days, run production traffic at 10% on the new class, run our benchmark suite and your smoke prompts). If perf/regressions are found, we will revert routing to A100 and provide a postmortem. Estimated migration effort: ~2 weeks for orchestration + one weekend maintenance window for KV cache warm-up.

- Model compatibility & quantization: most of your models can be run on H100 without re-quantizing. For aggressive int8 quantization we recommend a one-off regression eval; we budgeted 4 engineer-days in the proposal for tuning.

Attachments include: detailed perf/power/cost tables and a monthly pricing sheet with two term options (12m and 24m). We included a conservative throughput SLA credit schedule tied to reserved pool utilization.

If that looks reasonable I can circulate a DocuSign for the updated order and loop in Solutions Eng for a technical kickoff.

Best,

Jenna — quick technical notes to clarify numbers in Priya's proposal (forwarding summary):

> From the benchmark doc: H100 throughput advantage is workload-dependent. For your 16B conversational models at seq=512 & batch=8 we measured ~1.85x tokens/sec vs A100 (p95). For long-context runs (seq>2048) L40S shows stronger memory utilization and less KV cache fragmentation.

Specifics for your team to consider:
- KV cache warm-up: because we do prefix caching across the Dedicated pool, migration will see an initial latency bump for sessions that don't hit cache — we estimate this to settle within 48 hours for steady-state traffic.
- Batching policy: we recommend enabling adaptive batching with a max batch size of 16 for generation routes to retain latency targets while improving throughput.
- Quantization: we recommend running your embedder through our int8 qualification pipeline; in our test it reduced memory by ~30% with a <1.5% MRR impact. We budgeted a validation step and a canary evaluation in the quote.

Let us know any specific model names or datasets you want included in the regression set and we'll add them before sending to Procurement.

Avery Johnson
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
